**Tesla’s latest week‑long saga (Oct 9‑23 2026)**  

- **Cybertruck launch cancelled in Australia & New Zealand** – Tesla emailed customers on Oct 23 saying the highly‑anticipated Cybertruck will not be released in those markets [1].  
- **Flying Roadster unveiled** – On Oct 16–17 the company showed a “flying” version of the Roadster, claiming 0‑60 mph in under a second using SpaceX‑style thrusters; the reveal sparked viral videos and mixed investor reaction [14, 15, 16][17].  
- **Roadster production delayed to 2028** – Despite the demo, Elon Musk told traders that actual Roadster production won’t start until 2028, and prediction‑market participants remain skeptical after years of postponements [2].  
- **Full Self‑Driving rebranded in Europe** – Tesla renamed its FSD system “Tesla Assisted Driving” for the European market, a move noted on Oct 9 [19].  
- **Q3 profit plunge** – Reported on Oct 22, Tesla’s third‑quarter earnings fell 43%, underscoring financial pressure amid the rollout delays [8].  
- **Merger speculation with SpaceX** – Throughout Oct 21‑22, Musk publicly floated a potential Tesla‑SpaceX merger, prompting investor buzz, political betting ($366 M in campaign contributions), and warnings that his comments could invite shareholder scrutiny [4, 5, 6][10, 11].  
- **Safety incident with Full Self‑Driving** – A Tesla on FSD hit and killed a pedestrian on I‑80; dash‑cam footage showed the car attempted to brake and steer before the collision [7].  

*Overall picture*: Tesla is juggling bold product demos (flying Roadster), market setbacks (Cybertruck cancellation, profit drop, FSD rebrand), safety concerns, and high‑stakes merger talks with SpaceX—all within a two‑week window.
